Factorial affine GaG_{a}-varieties with principal plinth ideals

Kayo Masuda Address: Department of Mathematical Sciences, School of Science, Kwansei Gakuin University
1 Gakuen Uegahara, Sanda 669-1330, Japan Email address: kayo@kwansei.ac.jp
Abstract.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be a factorial affine variety defined over an algebraically closed field kk of characteristic zero with a nontrivial action of the additive group GaG_{a} associated to a locally nilpotent derivation δ\delta on BB. Suppose that A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta is an affine kk-domain. The quotient morphism π:X→Y=Spec​A\pi:X\to Y={\rm Spec}\;A splits to a composite pr∘p{\rm pr}\circ p of the projection pr:Y×𝔸1→Y{\rm pr}:Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\to Y and a GaG_{a}-equivariant birational morphism p:X→Y×𝔸1p:X\to Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where GaG_{a} acts on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} by translation. In this article, we study XX of dimension ≥3\geq 3 under the assumption that the plinth ideal δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A is a principal ideal generated by a non-unit element aa of AA. By decomposing p:X→Y×𝔸1p:X\to Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} to a sequence of GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications, we investigate the structure of XX. We show in algebraic way that the general closed fiber of π\pi over the closed set V⁡(a)V(a) of YY consists of a disjoint union of affine lines. The GaG_{a}-action on XX and the fixed-point locus XGaX^{G_{a}} are studied with particular interest.

Key words and phrases: 
additive group action, affine modification, 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-fibration
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary: 14R20; Secondary: 14R25, 13N15

1. Introduction

Let kk be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 00, which is the ground field. An affine algebraic variety XX is factorial iff the algebra of regular functions on XX is a UFD. Note that the algebra of regular functions on a smooth acyclic affine variety is a UFD [6]. Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be a factorial affine algebraic variety with a nontrivial algebraic action of the additive group GaG_{a}. There exists a nontrivial locally nilpotent derivation (abbreviated to lnd) δ\delta on BB associated to the GaG_{a}-action on XX. The fixed-point locus XGaX^{G_{a}} is defined by the ideal (δ⁡(B))(\delta(B)) generated by the image δ⁡(B)\delta(B). We assume that δ\delta is irreducible, i.e., δ⁡(B)\delta(B) is not contained in any proper principal ideal of BB. If codimX​XGa>1{\rm codim}_{X}X^{G_{a}}>1, then δ\delta is irreducible. Let A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta. Then AA coincides with the invariant ring BGaB^{G_{a}}. If dimX>3\dim X>3, AA is not necessarily finitely generated over kk. Suppose that AA is an affine kk-domain and let Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A. The quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y defined by the inclusion A↪BA\hookrightarrow B is an 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-fibration whose general closed fiber is a GaG_{a}-orbit 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. In fact, there exists an element z∈Bz\in B such that B⁡[a−1]=A⁡[a−1]​[z]B[a^{-1}]=A[a^{-1}][z] where a=δ⁡(z)∈A∖{0}a=\delta(z)\in A\setminus\{0\} and zz is transcendental over A⁡[a−1]A[a^{-1}]. Hence π|π−1​(D​(a)):π−1​(D⁡(a))→D⁡(a)\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(D(a))}:\pi^{-1}(D(a))\to D(a) is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle over the open set D⁡(a)={𝔭∈Spec​A∣𝔭∌a}D(a)=\{\mathfrak{p}\in{\rm Spec}\;A\mid\mathfrak{p}\not\ni a\}. Let p:X→Y×𝔸1=Spec​A​[z]p:X\to Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}={\rm Spec}\;A[z] be the GaG_{a}-equivariant morphism defined by the inclusion A⁡[z]↪BA[z]\hookrightarrow B. Then π\pi splits to π=pr∘p\pi={\rm pr}\circ p where pr:Y×𝔸1→Y{\rm pr}:Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\to Y is the projection. In [4], [5], Freudenburg defines the canonical factorization of the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y, which consists of pr:Y×𝔸1→Y{\rm pr}:Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\to Y and GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications developed by Kaliman and Zaidenberg [13]. Inspired by the work of Kaliman-Zaidenberg and Freudenburg, the GaG_{a}-action on XX of dimension ≥3\geq 3 is studied in [15] by decomposing the morphism p:X→Y×𝔸1p:X\to Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} to a sequence of GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications, and given is a criterion for XX to be isomorphic to a hypersurface of type xm​y−g⁡(z)=0x^{m}y-g(z)=0 where m>0m>0, xx is a prime element of AA and g⁡(z)∈A⁡[z]∖Ag(z)\in A[z]\setminus A. The ideal δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A of AA is called the plinth ideal. In this article, we study the structure of XX of dimension ≥3\geq 3 under the condition that the plinth ideal is principal. If XX and YY are smooth and if π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is surjective and equi-dimensional, the plinth ideal is principal (Lemma 2.1). Suppose that δ(B)∩A=α1p1⋯αspsA\delta(B)\cap A=\alpha_{1}^{p_{1}}\cdots\alpha_{s}^{p_{s}}A where α1,…,αs\alpha_{1},\ldots,\alpha_{s} are distinct prime elements of AA and pi>0p_{i}>0 for 1≤i≤s1\leq i\leq s. We decompose p:X→Y×𝔸1p:X\to Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} to a sequence of GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications

X=Xs→Xs−1→⋯→X1→Y×𝔸1.X=X_{s}\to X_{s-1}\to\cdots\to X_{1}\to Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}.

By investigating the affine modifications, we show that the general closed fiber of π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y over each V⁡(αi)=Spec​A/αi​AV(\alpha_{i})={\rm Spec}\;A/\alpha_{i}A consists of a disjoint union of mim_{i} affine lines for mi>1m_{i}>1 (Theorem 3.9). As a consequence, we obtain the following: Suppose that XX and YY are smooth and the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is surjective and equi-dimensional. Suppose, further, that the restriction π|π−1​(D​(a))\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(D(a))} is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle over an open set D⁡(a)D(a) of YY. If the general closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(a)=Y∖D⁡(a)V(a)=Y\setminus D(a) is irreducible, then π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle (Corollary 3.11). Hence XX is GaG_{a}-equivariantly isomorphic to Y×𝔸1Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where GaG_{a} acts on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} by translation. We also give a condition for XX to have no GaG_{a}-fixed points (Corollary 3.10).

For n≥3n\geq 3, an affine pseudo-nn-space is, by definition, a smooth affine variety ZZ equipped with a faithfully flat morphism q:Z→𝔸1=Spec​k​[x]q:Z\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}={\rm Spec}\;k[x] such that q−1​(𝔸∗1)≅𝔸∗1×𝔸n−1q^{-1}({\mathbb{A}}^{1}_{*})\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{1}_{*}\times{\mathbb{A}}^{n-1} and the scheme-theoretic fiber q∗​(0)q^{*}(0) is irreducible and reduced where 𝔸∗1=𝔸1∖{0}{\mathbb{A}}^{1}_{*}={\mathbb{A}}^{1}\setminus\{0\}. If X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B is an affine pseudo-nn-space, then XX is factorial with B∗=k∗B^{*}=k^{*} and has a GaG_{a}-action associated to an irreducible lnd δ\delta such that k⁡[x]⊂A=Ker​δk[x]\subset A={\rm Ker}\>\delta and δ⁡(B)∩A⊃xm​A\delta(B)\cap A\supset x^{m}A for some m>0m>0 [15]. Suppose that AA is an affine kk-domain and δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A is principal, and let Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A. By applying Corollary 3.11 to the affine pseudo-nn-space XX, we obtain that XX is GaG_{a}-equivariantly isomorphic to Y×𝔸1Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} if the general closed fiber of the quotient morphism π:X→Y=Spec​A\pi:X\to Y={\rm Spec}\;A over V⁡(x)V(x) is irreducible (Corollary 3.13). In particular, an affine pseudo-33-space X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B such that q∗​(0)=Spec​B/x​Bq^{*}(0)={\rm Spec}\;B/xB is factorial and (B/x​B)∗=k∗(B/xB)^{*}=k^{*} is isomorphic to Y×𝔸1≅𝔸3Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} if the general closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(x)V(x) is irreducible (Corollary 3.14). Then xx is a variable of X≅𝔸3X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} by a result of Kaliman [11]. If the general closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(x)V(x) is reducible, then XX is not necessarily isomorphic to Y×𝔸1Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} although X≅𝔸3X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} (see Example 4.1). We illustrate the GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications with examples in the last section.

2. Preliminaries

First, we recall some basic facts on lnds on an affine kk-domain. We refer to Miyanishi [17] and Freudenburg [4] for further details. For the quotient morphism by GaG_{a}-action, see also [9].

Let BB be an affine kk-domain and let δ\delta be a nontrivial lnd on BB. Let A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta. The group A∗A^{*} of invertibles of AA coincides with B∗B^{*}. If BB is factorial, then AA is factorial as well and a prime element of AA is a prime element of BB since AA is factorially closed in BB, i.e., x​y∈A∖{0}xy\in A\setminus\{0\} for x,y∈Bx,y\in B implies x,y∈Ax,y\in A. There exists an element z∈Bz\in B, called a local slice of δ\delta, which satisfies δ⁡(z)=a∈A∖{0}\delta(z)=a\in A\setminus\{0\}. It is well-known that B⁡[a−1]=A⁡[a−1]​[z]B[a^{-1}]=A[a^{-1}][z] and zz is transcendental over A⁡[a−1]A[a^{-1}]. If δ⁡(z)∈A∗\delta(z)\in A^{*}, zz is called a slice.

An lnd δ\delta is irreducible iff δ⁡(B)⊂b​B\delta(B)\subset bB for b∈Bb\in B implies b∈B∗b\in B^{*}. There exist a nontrivial irreducible lnd δ¯\bar{\delta} on BB and an element a∈Ker​δ¯∖{0}a\in{\rm Ker}\>\bar{\delta}\setminus\{0\} such that δ=a​δ¯\delta=a\bar{\delta}. Note that Ker​δ{\rm Ker}\>\delta coincides with Ker​δ¯{\rm Ker}\>\bar{\delta}.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B. The fixed point locus XGaX^{G_{a}} is defined by the ideal (δ⁡(B))(\delta(B)) generated by the image δ⁡(B)\delta(B). By a result of Bialynicki-Birula [1], XGaX^{G_{a}} has no isolated fixed points. If XX is factorial and δ\delta is irreducible, then XGaX^{G_{a}} has codimension >1>1.

The ideal δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A of AA is called the plinth ideal. An ideal II of BB is called δ\delta-stable or integral if δ⁡(I)⊂I\delta(I)\subset I.

When B=k[3]B=k^{[3]}, A=k[2]A=k^{[2]} by a result of Miyanishi [16] and the plinth ideal δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A is principal and the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y defined by the inclusion A↪BA\hookrightarrow B is surjective by Bonnet [2] (in case k=ℂk={\mathbb{C}}), Daigle and Kaliman [3] (in case that kk is of characteristic 00).

For elements a1,…,ara_{1},\ldots,a_{r} of a subdomain RR of BB, we denote by (a1,…,ar)​R(a_{1},\ldots,a_{r})R (resp. (a1,…,ar)​B(a_{1},\ldots,a_{r})B) the ideal of RR (resp. BB) generated by a1,…,ara_{1},\ldots,a_{r}. We have the following result.

Lemma 2.1.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be a smooth factorial affine variety with a GaG_{a}-action associated to an lnd δ\delta. Suppose that A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta is an affine kk-domain and Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A is smooth. If the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is surjective and equi-dimensional, then the plinth ideal δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A is principal.

Proof. Let a1,a2a_{1},a_{2} be nonzero elements of δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A such that ai=δ⁡(si)a_{i}=\delta(s_{i}) where si∈Bs_{i}\in B for i=1,2i=1,2. It suffices to show that d=gcd⁡(a1,a2)∈δ⁡(B)∩Ad=\gcd(a_{1},a_{2})\in\delta(B)\cap A. Let I=(a1,a2)​AI=(a_{1},a_{2})A. By the assumption, BB is faithfully flat over AA. Hence we have A∩I​B=IA\cap IB=I. Since δ⁡(a1​s2−a2​s1)=0\delta(a_{1}s_{2}-a_{2}s_{1})=0, it follows that a1​s2−a2​s1∈A∩I​B=Ia_{1}s_{2}-a_{2}s_{1}\in A\cap IB=I. Hence a1​s2−a2​s1=a1​c1−a2​c2a_{1}s_{2}-a_{2}s_{1}=a_{1}c_{1}-a_{2}c_{2} for c1,c2∈Ac_{1},c_{2}\in A. Then we have a1​(s2−c1)=a2​(s1−c2)a_{1}(s_{2}-c_{1})=a_{2}(s_{1}-c_{2}), hence a1′​(s2−c1)=a2′​(s1−c2)a^{\prime}_{1}(s_{2}-c_{1})=a^{\prime}_{2}(s_{1}-c_{2}) where ai=d​ai′a_{i}=da^{\prime}_{i} for i=1,2i=1,2. Define s=(s2−c1)/a2′=(s1−c2)/a1′s=(s_{2}-c_{1})/a^{\prime}_{2}=(s_{1}-c_{2})/a^{\prime}_{1}. Then s∈Bs\in B satisfies δ⁡(s)=d\delta(s)=d. Hence d∈δ⁡(B)∩Ad\in\delta(B)\cap A, and the assertion follows. ∎

For c∈B∖{0}c\in B\setminus\{0\}, we denote the localization of BB at cc by BcB_{c} or B⁡[c−1]B[c^{-1}].

Next, we review some basic facts of equivariant affine modifications of a factorial affine GaG_{a}-variety. We refer to Kaliman and Zaidenberg [13] for details.

Let BB be a factorial affine kk-domain. Let RR be a factorial subdomain of BB, II a nontrivial ideal of RR, and ff a nonzero element of II. The subalgebra of the quotient field Q⁡(R)Q(R) generated over RR by the elements a/fa/f for a∈Ia\in I is denoted by R⁡[f−1​I]R[f^{-1}I] and called the affine modification of RR along ff with center II. If II is generated by a1,…,ara_{1},\ldots,a_{r}, then

R⁡[f−1​I]=R⁡[a1/f,…,ar/f].R[f^{-1}I]=R[a_{1}/f,\ldots,a_{r}/f].

In particular, if II is generated by ff and gg which are coprime, then R⁡[f−1​I]=R⁡[g/f]R[f^{-1}I]=R[g/f] is isomorphic to R⁡[Y]/(f​Y−g)R[Y]/(fY-g) as an RR-algebra where R⁡[Y]=R[1]R[Y]=R^{[1]} (cf. [15]). Further, if RR is noetherian and II is a prime ideal, then R⁡[f−1​I]R[f^{-1}I] is factorial (ibid.).

Suppose that BB is equipped with a nontrivial lnd δ\delta restricting to RR. If II is δ\delta-stable and δ⁡(f)=0\delta(f)=0, then δ\delta uniquely lifts up to the affine modification R⁡[f−1​I]R[f^{-1}I]. Suppose, further, that B⁡[f−1]=R⁡[f−1]B[f^{-1}]=R[f^{-1}]. For i≥1i\geq 1, let IiI_{i} be the ideal R∩fi​BR\cap f^{i}B of RR and let Bi=R⁡[f−i​Ii]B_{i}=R[f^{-i}I_{i}]. Then there exsits a finite sequence of GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications

R=B0⊂B1⊂B2⊂⋯⊂Bμ=B.R=B_{0}\subset B_{1}\subset B_{2}\subset\cdots\subset B_{\mu}=B. (1)

where δ\delta restricts to BiB_{i} for 0≤i≤μ0\leq i\leq\mu (ibid). If BGa=RGaB^{G_{a}}=R^{G_{a}}, then BiGa=RGaB_{i}^{G_{a}}=R^{G_{a}} for every ii. The sequence (1) of GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications yields a GaG_{a}-equivariant birational morphisms

X=Xμ→Xμ−1→⋯→X1→X0X=X_{\mu}\to X_{\mu-1}\to\cdots\to X_{1}\to X_{0}

where Xi=Spec​BiX_{i}={\rm Spec}\;B_{i} for 0≤i≤μ0\leq i\leq\mu. We also call XiX_{i} a GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modification of X0X_{0}.

Let c∈R∖{0}c\in R\setminus\{0\} be an element such that δ⁡(c)=0\delta(c)=0 and ff and cc are coprime. By localizing the sequence (1) at cc, we have a sequence of GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications

Rc=B0,c⊂B1,c⊂B2,c⊂⋯⊂Bμ,c=BcR_{c}=B_{0,c}\subset B_{1,c}\subset B_{2,c}\subset\cdots\subset B_{\mu,c}=B_{c}

where Bi,c=Bi​[c−1]B_{i,c}=B_{i}[c^{-1}] for 0≤i≤μ0\leq i\leq\mu. For each ii, Bi,cB_{i,c} coincides with the GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modification of RcR_{c} along fif^{i} with center Ii,c=Rc∩fi​BcI_{i,c}=R_{c}\cap f^{i}B_{c}.

3. Equivariant affine modifications of factorial GaG_{a}-varieties

Let BB be a factorial affine kk-domain and let δ\delta be a nontrivial irreducible lnd on BB. Let A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta. Throughout this section, we assume that AA is noetherian and the plinth ideal is principal. Let

δ(B)∩A=α1p1α2p2⋯αspsA\delta(B)\cap A=\alpha_{1}^{p_{1}}\alpha_{2}^{p_{2}}\cdots\alpha_{s}^{p_{s}}A (3)

where αi\alpha_{i} is a prime element of AA, αi≠αj\alpha_{i}\neq\alpha_{j} if i≠ji\neq j, and pi>0p_{i}>0 for 1≤i≤s1\leq i\leq s. Let z∈Bz\in B be a local slice such that

δ(z)=α1p1α2p2⋯αsps.\delta(z)=\alpha_{1}^{p_{1}}\alpha_{2}^{p_{2}}\cdots\alpha_{s}^{p_{s}}.

Corollary 3.10.

Suppose that δ⁡(B)∩A=αp​A\delta(B)\cap A=\alpha^{p}A for a prime element α∈A\alpha\in A and p>0p>0. With the notation above, the following assertions hold.

Corollary 3.11.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be a smooth factorial affine variety with a GaG_{a}-action associated to an irreducible lnd δ\delta. Suppose that A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta is an affine kk-domain and Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A is smooth. Suppose further that the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is surjective and equi-dimensional, and the restriction π|π−1​(D​(a)):π−1​(D⁡(a))→D⁡(a)\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(D(a))}:\pi^{-1}(D(a))\to D(a) is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle for a nonzero a∈Aa\in A. If the general closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(a)V(a) is irreducible, then π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle. Hence XX is equivariantly isomorphic to Y×𝔸1Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where GaG_{a} acts trivially on YY and by translation on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}.

Proof. By Lemma 2.1, δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A is a principal ideal. If δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A is a unit ideal, then there exsits a slice of δ\delta and B=A[1]B=A^{[1]}, i.e., π\pi is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle. Suppose that δ⁡(B)∩A=a′​A\delta(B)\cap A=a^{\prime}A for a non-unit a′∈Aa^{\prime}\in A. Let a1∈Aa_{1}\in A be any prime factor of a′a^{\prime}. If V⁡(a1)⊄V⁡(a)V(a_{1})\not\subset V(a), then the general closed fiber over V⁡(a1)V(a_{1}) consists of a single 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} since π|π−1​(D​(a))\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(D(a))} is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle. However, this is a conrtadiction by Theorem 3.9. Hence V⁡(a1)⊂V⁡(a)V(a_{1})\subset V(a), and it follows that V⁡(a′)⊂V⁡(a)V(a^{\prime})\subset V(a). Since the general closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(a)V(a) is irreducible by the assumption, this is a contradiction again by Theorem 3.9. Hence the assertion follows. ∎

We apply the results obrained so far to an affine pseudo-nn-space. Let n≥3n\geq 3. An affine pseudo-nn-space X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B is a smooth affine algebraic variety equipped with a faithfully flat morphism q:X→𝔸1=Spec​k​[x]q:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}={\rm Spec}\;k[x] such that q−1​(𝔸∗1)≅𝔸∗1×𝔸n−1q^{-1}({\mathbb{A}}^{1}_{*})\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{1}_{*}\times{\mathbb{A}}^{n-1} and q∗​(0)q^{*}(0) is irreducible and reduced. Then BB is factorial, B∗=k∗B^{*}=k^{*}, and xx is a prime element of BB by [15]. The following can be proved by the same argument in [8, Theorem 2.3].

Theorem 3.12.

([8, Theorem 2.3]) Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be an affine pseudo-nn-space with a faithfully flat morphism q:X→𝔸1=Spec​k​[x]q:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}={\rm Spec}\;k[x]. Assume that X0=q∗​(0)X_{0}=q^{*}(0) is smooth. Then the following conditions are equivalent.

  1. (1)

    XX is contractible.

  2. (2)

    XX is acyclic, i.e., Hi​(X,ℤ)=0H_{i}(X;{\mathbb{Z}})=0 for every i>0i>0.

  3. (3)

    X0X_{0} is acyclic.

By the trivialization q−1​(𝔸∗1)≅𝔸∗1×𝔸n−1q^{-1}({\mathbb{A}}^{1}_{*})\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{1}_{*}\times{\mathbb{A}}^{n-1}, XX has an algebraic action of Gan−1G_{a}^{n-1} associated to commuting irreducible lnds δ1,…,δn−1\delta_{1},\ldots,\delta_{n-1} such that ∩i=1n−1Kerδi=k[x]\cap_{i=1}^{n-1}{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{i}=k[x]. For each ii, there exsits a local slice zi∈Bz_{i}\in B such that δi​(zi)=xpi\delta_{i}(z_{i})=x^{p_{i}} for pi≥0p_{i}\geq 0 [15]. Take any lnd δi\delta_{i} and let δ=δi\delta=\delta_{i}. Then XX has a GaG_{a}-action corresponding to δ\delta and q:X→𝔸1q:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is GaG_{a}-equivariant. Suppose that A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta is an affine kk-domain. Then qq splits to q=τ∘πq=\tau\circ\pi where π:X→Y=Spec​A\pi:X\to Y={\rm Spec}\;A is the quotient morphism and τ:Y→𝔸1=Spec​k​[x]\tau:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}={\rm Spec}\;k[x] is the morphism induced by the inclusion k⁡[x]↪Ak[x]\hookrightarrow A. If YY is smooth and π\pi is surjective and equi-dimensional, δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A is principal by Lemma 2.1 and δ⁡(B)∩A=xp​A\delta(B)\cap A=x^{p}A for p≥0p\geq 0. Applying Corollary 3.11 to an affine pseudo-nn-space XX, we have the following.

Corollary 3.13.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be an affine pseudo-nn-space with a faithfully flat morphism q:X→𝔸1=Spec​k​[x]q:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}={\rm Spec}\;k[x] and a GaG_{a}-action such that q:X→𝔸1q:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is GaG_{a}-equivariant where GaG_{a} acts trivially on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. Let δ\delta be the irreducible lnd on BB corresponding to the GaG_{a}-action and let A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta. Suppose that AA is an affine kk-domain and Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A is smooth. Suppose further that the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is surjective and equi-dimensional. If the general closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(x)V(x) is irreducible, then XX is GaG_{a}-equivariantly isomorphic to Y×𝔸1Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where GaG_{a} acts on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} by translation.

For an affine pseudo-33-space XX, the following holds.

Corollary 3.14.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be as in Corollary 3.13 with n=3n=3. Suppose that q∗​(0)q^{*}(0) is factorial with (B/x​B)∗=k∗(B/xB)^{*}=k^{*}. Then X≅𝔸3X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} and xx is a variable. Further, if the general closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(x)V(x) is irreducible, then X≅Y×𝔸1X\cong Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A with A=BGa=k​[x][1]A=B^{G_{a}}=k[x]^{[1]}.

Proof. As shown above, there exist an irreducible lnd δ\delta and z∈Bz\in B such that δ⁡(z)=xp1\delta(z)=x^{p_{1}} for p1≥0p_{1}\geq 0. The kernel A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta is k​[x][1]k[x]^{[1]} by [15, Lemma 5.1]. Since q∗​(0)=Spec​B/x​Bq^{*}(0)={\rm Spec}\;B/xB is factorial with a nontrivial GaG_{a}-action induced by δ\delta and (B/x​B)∗=k∗(B/xB)^{*}=k^{*}, it follows that q∗​(0)≅𝔸2q^{*}(0)\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{2}, and hence q∗​(0)q^{*}(0) is smooth and acyclic. Then XX is acyclic by Theorem 3.12. Since q∗​(0)q^{*}(0) is factorial, X≅𝔸3X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} and xx is a variable by a result of Kaliman [11]. Also by [10], π:X→Y=Spec​A≅𝔸2\pi:X\to Y={\rm Spec}\;A\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{2} is surjective and equi-dimensional. Hence the plinth ideal δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A is principal by Lemma 2.1 and generated by xpx^{p} for p≥0p\geq 0. If the general closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(x)V(x) is irreducible, X≅Y×𝔸1X\cong Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} by Corollary 3.13. ∎

In Corollary 3.14, if the general closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(x)V(x) is reducible, then XX is not necessarily isomorphic to Y×𝔸1Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} as shown in Example 4.1 below, although X≅𝔸3X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3}.

4. Examples

We illustrate affine modifications of GaG_{a}-varieties by examples.

The closed fiber of π\pi over V⁡(F)∖V⁡(F,G)V(F)\setminus V(F,G) consists of 55 affine lines, the one over V⁡(G)∖V⁡(F,G)V(G)\setminus V(F,G) consists of 22 affine lines, and the one over V⁡(F,G)V(F,G) is 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} with multiplicity 1010, which is the fixed-point locus. The canonical factorization of XX is explicitly given by Freudenburg in [5];

A=k⁡[F,G]⊂A⁡[R]=\displaystyle A=k[F,G]\subset A[R]= k⁡[F,G,R]⊂k⁡[F,G,R,x]\displaystyle k[F,G,R]\subset k[F,G,R,x]
⊂k⁡[F,R,x,S]⊂k⁡[F,x,S,y]⊂k⁡[x,y,z]=B.\displaystyle\subset k[F,R,x,S]\subset k[F,x,S,y]\subset k[x,y,z]=B.

The subsequence A⁡[R]⊂⋯⊂BA[R]\subset\cdots\subset B of the canonical factorization consists of GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications.

Our sequences of GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications can provide the information on the singular fibers of the quotient morphism in a direct way.
